facts:
Games: levels 2-4 use the Gamelytics dataset (Kaggle): an unnamed mobile game, 1 million registrations 1998-2020, 9.6 million logins, and a 404,770-player shop (offer set) A/B test. The data looks simulated, so treat it as practice data. Level 1's gate experiment uses Cookie Cats (Kaggle), a real match-3 puzzle game by Tactile Entertainment, 90,189 new players.
Window: players who registered 2020-01-01 to 2020-09-22: 353,915 new players.
Onboarding: 76.0% never come back after day one; 24.0% come back within 7 days, and nobody returns for the first time after day 7. Median first return: day 4. Cookie Cats: 38.0% play fewer than 10 rounds in 14 days; 4.4% never play a round. Players with 100+ rounds return on day 7 about 71% of the time vs about 2% for 1-9 rounds.
Gate test (Cookie Cats): moving the first gate from level 30 to 40 changed day-1 retention by -0.6 points (p=0.074, could be luck) and day-7 retention by -0.8 points (p=0.002, a real difference). Recommendation: keep it at 30.
Retention: day 1 2.0%, day 3 4.6%, day 7 5.8%, day 14 4.6%, day 30 2.9%. Peak is day 6 at 6.9%. Weekly cohorts are flat.
Engagement: about 15,461 players a day recently (vs 10,453 in January); 102,241 monthly players; stickiness (DAU/MAU) 15.5%.
Player kinds (first 30 days): Tried once (0 days back): 76.0% of players, 33.2% of visits; Visitors (1-3 days): 5.7% of players, 7.4% of visits; Regulars (4-7 days): 14.2% of players, 42.5% of visits; Superfans (8+ days): 4.1% of players, 16.9% of visits.
Shop test: shop A (old) vs shop B (new). Buy rate 1.0% vs 0.9% (p=0.035, real difference, B lower). Money per player 25.41 vs 26.75 (p=0.51, could be luck). Money per buyer 2,664 vs 3,004. Typical buyer spends 311 (A) vs 3,022 (B). Shop A has 123 huge spenders (10,000+) bringing 89.4% of its money; shop B has none. Without them B wins by 24.05 per player.
Player reviews: 25,719 Google Play reviews of 9 match-3 games, average 3.24 stars, 35% are 1-2 stars. Themes far more common in 1-2 star than 4-5 star reviews: too hard/stuck 4.1x, bugs & crashes 3.3x, lost progress 3.0x, rewards & boosters 2.2x, prices/pay-to-win 2.1x, ads 1.8x. 'Fun & relaxing' is the top delight. Ads are the #1 complaint for 3 of 9 competitors; Match Masters' #1 complaint is boosters.
Recommendations: fix the first session and add a day-1 reason to return; get players through their first 10 rounds; keep the gate at level 30; don't ship shop B as-is, add a high-value bundle and re-test; audit the 123 huge spenders; a streak reward to turn Regulars into Superfans; track revenue concentration next to ARPU.
Dashboard tabs: Home, Level 1 Starting, Level 2 Coming back, Level 3 Playing, Level 4 Spending, Power-up lab (what-if planner), and the Neon Dash mini-game. Made by Jatin Chauhan.
